events.title: Netlify launched
events.summary: Mathias Biilmann and Christian Bach publicly launched Netlify on April 7, 2015 — a Git-based platform for deploying static sites and JAMstack apps to a global CDN.
events.about: Netlify connected Git pushes to automatic builds and CDN deploys — no server configuration. It coined the JAMstack term and became the default hosting layer for Gatsby, Hugo, and later Next.js static exports before Vercel dominated React SSR.

narrative.whyChosen: Netlify pioneered Git-to-CDN deploys for static and JAMstack sites.
narrative.whyImportant: It made frontend deploys as simple as `git push` for thousands of developers.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams manually FTP'd build artifacts or managed nginx configs for every static site.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy S6 released
events.summary: Samsung began selling the Samsung Galaxy S6 — glass-and-metal redesign dropped removable battery for premium build quality.
events.about: The Galaxy S series remained [Android]'s volume flagship counterweight to iPhone. Glass-and-metal redesign dropped removable battery for premium build quality. Developers testing [Android] builds routinely validated on Galaxy S hardware as the default non-[Pixel] reference.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy S6 continued Samsung's annual [Android] flagship cadence.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy S devices set the hardware bar millions of [Android] users and developers encounter.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] needed consistent premium hardware for testing flagship features each year.

events.title: Apple Watch released
events.summary: Apple began selling the Apple Watch on April 24, 2015 — a smartwatch running watchOS with a new app [SDK] and Digital Crown input.
events.about: watchOS brought Swift/UIKit extensions to the wrist — complications, health sensors, and glanceable notifications. Developers built companion apps paired with iPhone backends; Apple later added cellular models and native App Store distribution on-watch. It opened wearable computing as a mainstream platform beyond fitness bands.

narrative.whyChosen: The Apple Watch launched watchOS as a first-class Apple developer platform.
narrative.whyImportant: It created a new form factor for companion apps, health APIs, and glanceable [UI] patterns.
narrative.problemSolved: Users wanted smartphone notifications and health tracking without pulling a phone from their pocket.

events.title: Caddy first released
events.summary: Matt Holt released Caddy v0.5.0 on April 28, 2015 — a Go web server with [HTTP]/2 support and a simple configuration format.
events.about: Caddy later added automatic Let's Encrypt [HTTPS] (from v0.8 in December 2015) — `caddy reverse-proxy` could terminate [TLS] without manual certbot steps. Its Caddyfile config and JSON [API] made it popular for dev proxies, static sites, and [API] gateways.

narrative.whyChosen: Caddy made automatic [HTTPS] a default feature, not an afterthought.
narrative.whyImportant: It showed a modern web server could be simple, secure, and written in Go.
narrative.problemSolved: Configuring [TLS] certificates and [HTTP]/2 on nginx or Apache remained painful for small teams.

events.title: Visual Studio Code preview released
events.summary: Microsoft released the Visual Studio Code preview on April 29, 2015 — a free, cross-platform editor with IntelliSense, debugging, and Git integration.
events.about: VS Code is the default editor for millions of developers — TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, and more via extensions. It is Electron-based but keyboard-centric: multi-cursor editing, integrated terminal, [debugger], and Git diff view. It displaced Atom and challenged JetBrains for everyday editing.

narrative.whyChosen: VS Code proved Microsoft could win developer mindshare with a free, cross-platform editor.
narrative.whyImportant: It became the hub for LSP-based language support and the most popular dev tool in surveys.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers on Mac and Linux lacked a lightweight Microsoft-grade editor with solid debugging and Git.
